source_caption:
10 Things I Hate About You is a high school romantic comedy set in Seattle, loosely inspired by The Taming of the Shrew by William Shakespeare. The story follows Kat Stratford, a smart but rebellious teen who refuses to date, while her younger sister Bianca is only allowed to date if Kat does too. To get around this rule, Bianca’s admirer arranges for the mysterious and edgy Patrick Verona to date Kat. What starts as a scheme slowly turns into something more real, as Patrick begins to genuinely care for her.

The film stands out for its witty dialogue, strong female lead, and memorable performances by Heath Ledger and Julia Stiles. It mixes humor with emotional depth, especially in scenes where Kat reveals her vulnerability beneath her tough exterior. With its iconic moments, like Patrick singing in the school stadium, the movie became a defining teen rom-com of the late ’90s and remains popular for its relatable themes of love, identity, and teenage rebellion.

source_details.synopsis: 10 Things I Hate About You is a 1999 American teen romantic comedy directed by Gil Junger (in his directorial debut) from a screenplay by Karen McCullah Lutz and Kirsten Smith. Adapted from William Shakespeare's comedy The Taming of the Shrew, it stars Julia Stiles, Heath Ledger, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Larisa Oleynik, Larry Miller, Andrew Keegan, David Krumholtz, Susan May Pratt, and Gabrielle Union. In the film, high-school student Cameron James (Gordon-Levitt) is unable to date sophomore Bianca Stratford (Oleynik) until her asocial feminist senior sister Kat (Stiles) dates, leading to Cameron recruiting bad boy classmate Patrick Verona (Ledger) to date Kat.
